restatements.text: Requires all county jails to hold individuals named in federal immigration detainer requests for up to 48 hours beyond their normal release time.

analysis.answer: Currently, each county decides whether to honor federal immigration detainers. This measure mandates that every county jail must honor them by holding individuals up to 48 hours past their normal release time.

Direct costs include housing and feeding detainees for up to 48 extra hours. Opportunity costs involve jail space and staff time diverted from other duties. There may be legal costs for counties if lawsuits arise over the legality of the extended detention.

County governments bear the financial and administrative costs of the extended detention. Federal immigration authorities benefit by gaining more time to take custody of individuals without expending federal detention resources upfront.

Counties may face increased liability risk and might alter standard release practices to manage jail capacity. Federal authorities will likely issue more detainers knowing they will be honored uniformly across the state. Civil liberties organizations may file lawsuits challenging the 48-hour holds as unconstitutional seizures.

It addresses a lack of uniform cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities by imposing a statewide mandate. While this mechanism removes local "sanctuary" policies, it creates a new unfunded mandate for local jails and extends detention without judicial warrants.

Federal immigration authorities gain the power to keep people detained in local custody based solely on an administrative request. The state gains uniform control over local jail policies regarding immigration.

Researchers disagree on the effects of local cooperation with immigration enforcement. Some find it improves public safety by facilitating the removal of offenders, while others find it reduces public safety by making immigrant communities less likely to report crimes to local police.
Administrative costs will arise from coordinating handoffs, processing paperwork between local jail staff and federal agents, and managing jail bed availability.

flags.quote: Every county jail shall honor a detainer request from federal immigration authorities by holding the named person for up to 48 hours
flags.note: The measure requires county jails to hold individuals longer, incurring housing and staffing costs, without providing state funding to cover those costs.
